title: Why had the Holy Ghost not yet fallen on the Samaritans who were baptized?
summary: Acts 8:12 says the Samaritans “believed Philip” and “were baptized”. Acts 8:16 says that “as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus”, and 8:14–17 has Peter and John come down, pray, and lay hands on them, and “they received the Holy Ghost”. The passage does not say why the Spirit had not come on them before that.
text: KJV Acts 8:12: “they believed Philip preaching” … “they were baptized, both men and women”. KJV Acts 8:16: “as yet he was fallen upon none of them”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Acts 8:16: οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός [for he had not yet fallen upon any of them]. KJV Acts 8:17: “Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/44/8/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/44/8/.
reasoning: The text gives two facts side by side: they had believed and been baptized, and the Spirit had not fallen on any of them until the apostles came. It does not say what the gap was meant to show or what was lacking. Different readings are held as possibilities only: that the Spirit was given through the apostles’ hands in this case for a purpose tied to Samaria, that belief and baptism are distinct from the receiving, or that the delay was particular to this occasion. The text does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Acts 8:12–17. The record does not say which reading is right, does not say that this account differs from any other account in the book, and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. The Greek quoted is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life, and the Textus Receptus text served was not quoted here. The Greek New Testament wording is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life (TISCH), compared with the Textus Receptus text served there (TR); neither is a critical apparatus.

title: How were Paul and his company “forbidden of the Holy Ghost” to preach in Asia?
summary: Acts 16:6 says that Paul and those with him “were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia”, and 16:7 says that when they tried to go into Bithynia “the Spirit suffered them not”. The next verse of the passage that gives a direction is a vision of a man of Macedonia (16:9). The passage does not say by what means the prohibition came.
text: KJV Acts 16:6: “were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Acts 16:6: κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ [prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the word in Asia]. KJV Acts 16:7: “they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not”. KJV Acts 16:9: “a vision appeared to Paul in the night”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/44/16/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/44/16/.
reasoning: The passage names the agent, the Holy Spirit, and the places, Asia and Bithynia, but not the means. Different readings are held as possibilities only: a spoken or inward word, a prophetic utterance by someone in the company, or a hindrance in events. The next direction in the passage is stated as a vision (16:9), but the text does not say that the earlier ones came the same way.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Acts 16:6–9. The record does not say which reading is right, and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more about how the Spirit directed the apostles. The Greek quoted is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life; the Textus Receptus text served was not quoted here, and the reading “the Spirit of Jesus” at 16:7 is the subject of a separate record. title: Whose vow was it at Cenchrea, and what was it?
summary: Acts 18:18 says that Paul sailed into Syria “and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow”. The verse does not say whether “he” is Paul or Aquila, and does not say what the vow was, to whom it was made or for what.
text: KJV Acts 18:18: “and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Acts 18:18: κειράμενος ἐν Κενχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν, εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν [having shorn the head in Cenchrea, for he had a vow]. KJV Acts 21:23: “We have four men which have a vow on them”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/44/18/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/44/18/.
reasoning: The verse has one participle for the shaving and one verb for the vow, both singular and masculine, set after the names of Priscilla and Aquila, so the verse does not settle whether Paul or Aquila is meant. The vow itself is not described. Different readings are held as possibilities only: that it was Paul’s own vow and a vow of a kind spoken of in Acts 21:23, or Aquila’s, or a vow of another kind. The text does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Acts 18:18, with Acts 21:23 quoted only as another place where the book mentions a vow. The record does not say which reading is right, does not say that the two vows are of one kind, and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more.
